purpose: Check whether the NGA Geographic Names Server independently resolves the literature locality phrase Rogo Point in the Philippines, without treating a name search as a boundary or fish-occurrence source.

source.provider: National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, Geographic Names Server
source.citationRecommendation: Toponymic information is based on the Geographic Names Database, containing official standard names approved by the United States Board on Geographic Names and maintained by the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.
source.importantDisclaimer: NGA describes GNS data as guidance/general-public information, notes names may not reflect sovereignty views, and disclaims responsibility for third-party uses of feature coordinates. This is not a Philippine legal or maritime boundary source.

queries.name: all-name-contains
queries.interpretation: Broad substring matches include unrelated names and multiple name rows for shared features; none is Rogo Point or a Ragay Gulf feature.

decision.reason: The exact-name query returned zero records; broader substring queries returned only unrelated name rows. A missing GNS match cannot establish that Rogo Point does not exist, is not recorded in another source, or lies outside any province.

limitations: GNS is a supplementary geographic-name reference, not a Philippine agency source and not a legal, hydrographic, provincial, or municipal-water boundary dataset.
The queried name fields do not identify the 1966 CAS 47780 collection position or establish which side of Ragay Gulf the point/locality refers to.
No coordinates or geometries were requested or included in the tracked review.
The historical ZooKeys type locality is not current fish-presence evidence, a complete inventory, a catchability statement, or fishing-access guidance.
nextAction: Keep Rogo Point unresolved. Seek the 1966 cruise station log or an appropriate NAMRIA hydrographic chart/source that explicitly names the point; continue independent CALABARZON freshwater and marine evidence work without assigning the whole gulf to one region.
